task_message:
Case V01: segment the vascular soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 131x131x139 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case V01 finished. 

**Summary of the work:**
- **Overview:** Opened the case (T2-weighted 1 mm isotropic MRI of a hand/distal forearm) and scanned all three planes with contact sheets to locate the abnormality. The limb runs distally (digits) → proximally (forearm) along the axial axis.
- **Lesion identification:** Found a well-circumscribed, mildly T2-hyperintense soft-tissue mass in the soft tissues at the metacarpal level (approximately 3.4 × 1.9 × 3.3 cm), clearly asymmetric relative to the opposite side of the hand, with a capsule-like border visible in axial, coronal and sagittal planes.
- **Segmentation:** Seeded the mass with a positive point (→ v1, 8.7 mL), then applied a model refine (→ v2, 8.4 mL) which tightened the boundary.
- **Verification:** Checked the mask against the lesion edge on multiple axial (76, 80, 85, 90, 91, 104), coronal (72, 78, 81, 84, 86) and sagittal (44, 46, 48, 56) slices; the outline follows the mass capsule and tapers at both ends. Automatic candidates C1 (25 mL) and C2 (15 mL) were rejected as they enclosed normal bones, muscles and fat.
- **Final:** Saved mask v2 (8.4 mL, single component) with medium confidence, since the lesion boundary is consistent in all three planes but the mass borders bulky normal soft tissue.
